items.title: Accurate and Auditable ECG Classification via Visibility Graph Neural Networks
items.abstract: Physicians read electrocardiograms (ECGs) from waveform shape and timing, yet accurate deep-learning classifiers rarely show which waveform regions drive their predictions. We introduce LYNX-ECG, a graph neural network that represents each heartbeat as a sparse visibility graph of timestamped turning points. On CODE-Test, LYNX-ECG reaches a macro F1 score of 0.889, outperforming five baselines including the ECGFounder foundation model, while its graphs need about 14% of the storage of graphs built from every sample. Because each node maps to a specific ECG time, we can delete clinically defined waveform regions and alter beat timing to audit predictions. For conduction disorders, the clinically expected region was the strongest evidence in more than 90% of correct predictions. Bradycardia and tachycardia calls follow heart rate with conduction intervals held fixed, and atrial fibrillation calls vanish when beat-to-beat variation is removed. Sparse visibility graphs thus pair accurate ECG classification with clinically grounded, testable explanations.

items.title: Advances in Alzheimer’s disease diagnosis and therapeutic strategies: an integrative review of current evidence.
items.abstract: Alzheimer's disease is the leading cause of dementia worldwide and represents one of the greatest challenges facing contemporary medicine because of its high prevalence, irreversible progression, and profound impact on patients, their families, and healthcare systems. The present study aimed to analyze recent scientific advances in the diagnosis and therapeutic strategies for Alzheimer's disease through an integrative review of specialized literature. To achieve this objective, a qualitative analysis of scientific publications was conducted. The findings reveal a significant transformation in the diagnostic paradigm, shifting from an approach based primarily on clinical assessment to one supported by biological biomarkers, advanced neuroimaging techniques, and precision medicine strategies capable of identifying neuropathological changes during the preclinical stages of the disease. Likewise, the literature demonstrates a substantial shift in treatment approaches, moving from symptomatic management toward interventions designed to modify disease progression. Important advances were also identified in the fields of artificial intelligence, nanotechnology, precision pharmacology, and the development of innovative drug discovery platforms. Although significant challenges remain regarding biological heterogeneity, clinical efficacy, safety, accessibility, and the implementation of these innovations, the available scientific evidence indicates that the future management of Alzheimer's disease will be based on early diagnosis, molecular patient stratification, and the development of personalized therapeutic strategies capable of delaying neurodegeneration and improving clinical outcomes.

items.title: Advancing Mental Health Support Through Orange Technology and Empathetic Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: Mental health systems face a persistent gap in accessible, continuous, and person-centred support. Conversational AI can expand access to psychoeducation, emotional check-ins, self-management, and service navigation, but may also introduce risks of digital exclusion, cultural mismatch, privacy concerns, unsafe advice, and overreliance on automation. This paper develops a conceptual framework integrating Orange Technology, which promotes emotional wellbeing, cultural sensitivity, social connectedness, and resilience, with empathetic AI for mental health support. An integrative literature review examined peer-reviewed systematic reviews and WHO and UN guidance published from 2021 to 2026. Evidence suggests that conversational AI can improve depression, distress, anxiety, and engagement, although effects are heterogeneous and may decline over time. Personalization and empathic interaction may enhance engagement, while the framework's effects on community resilience, cultural sensitivity, and community resource integration require further empirical validation. The framework therefore positions AI as a supportive, human-in-the-loop layer rather than a replacement for clinicians, families, peers, or communities. It connects emotional sensing, empathetic dialogue, personalized support, escalation pathways, community connection, inclusive access, and governance, while aligning mental health innovation with SDG 3, 9, and 17.

items.title: Adversarial-resilient iot-enabled financial intelligence system using explainable deep learning for sentiment-driven stock trading decisions
items.abstract: Financial stock market trend decision systems support the investment decisions by predicting future price movements and analyzing large-scale market data. Despite, IoT enabled trading systems continuously collects and exchange sentiment and market information are exposed to adversarial attacks, which misleads automated trading algorithms and results in inaccurate investment decision systems. To face this challenge, this study proposes an adversarial-resilient explainable artificial intelligence for sentiment-driven stock trading (ARXAI-SST) architecture. The proposed framework combines graph neural networks (GNN) for adversarial attack detection, FinBERT based sentiment representation, BiLSTM with attention (BiLSTM-Att) for the sentiment analysis, and SHAP-based explainable artificial intelligence for enhancing model interpretability. The experimentation outcomes show that the proposed framework accomplishes higher accuracy and robustness compared with the existing approaches while providing transparent insights into the trading decisions. The proposed model offers an efficient and reliable solution for secure sentiment driven stock trading in IoT enabled financial environments.

items.title: Affective Education and the Pedagogy of Desire for Teacher Training in the Digital Affective Era
items.abstract: In today's educational landscape, deeply marked by the neoliberal logic of performance and an obsession with digital self-promotion, a structural pedagogical crisis is becoming increasingly evident. Schools, traditionally understood as symbolic places of encounter, mediation and the transmission of values, now face a radical challenge: to rethink themselves, their tools and their languages in order to respond to profoundly changed educational needs. It is against this backdrop that our reflection begins, with a question intended to run through the entire discussion proposed here like a common thread: is it really possible that human beings – and, with them, educators – could be replaced by artificial intelligence in the emotional and educational spheres? And, above all, what human characteristic will no digital algorithm ever be able to replicate? The starting point for this analysis is a description of a twofold crisis affecting the contemporary world. items.title: AGENTIC ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AS A TOOL FOR IMPROVING OPERATIONAL EFFICIENCY AND TRANSFORMING ENTERPRISE BUSINESS MODELS
items.abstract: This article examines agentic artificial intelligence as an emerging class of technologies that fundamentally reshapes business process automation, shifting the paradigm from reactive assistant systems to autonomous solutions capable of independent planning, decision-making, and execution of multi-step actions within defined authority boundaries. The aim of this study stems from a growing realization that traditional AI implementation strategies are failing to deliver expected returns. This discrepancy between strategic ambitions and practical outcomes calls for a systematic investigation of alternative approaches to AI integration, particularly those offering higher autonomy and operational transformation potential. The study demonstrates that agentic AI fundamentally transforms the cost structure of business operations by converting variable labor expenses into predominantly fixed and highly scalable technology costs, thereby altering the economics of enterprise operations. The analysis reveals that organizations implementing agentic AI achieve dramatic operational improvements including task completion time reductions and significant cost optimizations through the elimination of manual inefficiencies. The findings further show that successful scaling of agentic systems depends not so much on technological excellence as on organizational readiness, in particular the development of appropriate governance frameworks for managing autonomous systems, ensuring transparency and explainability in automated decision-making, and integrating AI agents effectively into hybrid human-machine teams while addressing workforce skill gaps. The practical value of this research lies in providing business leaders and technology managers with actionable insights for strategic decision-making regarding AI investments, offering a systematic framework for evaluating deployment opportunities across different business functions, understanding critical success factors that differentiate successful implementations from failed pilots, and anticipating organizational changes required for effective integration. The conclusions provide direction for bridging the persistent gap between AI technological capabilities and practical business outcomes, while outlining promising avenues for future research into economic impact longer-term socioeconomic consequences of widespread AI adoption on workforce composition and organizational structures.

items.title: AgentShield: Fortifying Web Applications Against AI Agents and Agentic Browsers
items.abstract: LLM-powered browser agents are transforming web automation by autonomously interacting with websites and executing complex workflows. However, the effectiveness of existing anti-bot defenses against these systems remains unclear. We present a systematic empirical evaluation of modern agentic browsers against widely deployed anti-bot mechanisms, characterizing their capabilities, limitations, and behavioral differences from humans. Our results show that many defenses designed for traditional automation struggle to reliably detect autonomous AI-driven agents. Accordingly, we introduce AgentShield, a behavioral fingerprinting framework that targets the Perception-Reasoning-Action (PRA) loop underlying agentic user clients. By leveraging dynamic web forms that progressively reveal content and capture fine-grained interaction telemetry, AgentShield exposes behavioral artifacts that enable differentiation between human users and autonomous agents. We further demonstrate Extinction-induced Policy Drift (EPD), a novel attack in which repeated obstruction of task completion causes agents to relax their safeguards and engage in unsafe behaviors. Finally, we present defensive prompt injection techniques that exploit agent-specific weaknesses to mitigate emerging forms of autonomous web abuse that rely on content extraction. Our results highlight both the shortcomings of current web defenses against agentic user clients and the feasibility of practical detection mechanisms tailored to this new generation of web automation.

items.title: AI Agents and Corporate Liability: A Comparative Policy Analysis for Business Law Reform in India
items.abstract: Abstract The emergence of autonomous AI agents, which can independently negotiate contracts, conduct financial transactions, manage customer interactions, and make business decisions with minimal human involvement, has ushered in a revolutionary era for Artificial Intelligence (AI). They promise greater efficiency and innovation, but also expose serious gaps in traditional legal doctrines of corporate liability that assume human agency, intention, and control. Recent events such as the Air Canada chatbot litigation, Robodebt in Australia, and Childcare Benefits Scandal in the Netherlands show that autonomous algorithmic decisions can lead to contract disputes, discriminatory outcomes, consumer detriment, financial loss, and institutional failures, raising fundamental questions of corporate accountability and legal responsibility. The paper seeks to critically analyze whether the existing legal framework in India, i.e., the Companies Act, 2013, the Indian Contract Act, 1872, the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, the Information Technology Act, 2000, and the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, can deal with the liability arising due to autonomous AI agents making commercial decisions. This study adopts doctrinal, comparative, and policy-oriented legal research methods to examine emerging international regulatory approaches, such as the European Union AI Act, the OECD AI Principles, ISO/IEC 42001 Artificial Intelligence Management Systems, and Singapore’s AI Governance Framework, with a view to identifying global best practices for responsible AI governance. The paper argues that traditional fault-based liability is increasingly ill-suited to situations in which artificial intelligence systems independently influence corporate decisions. It proposes a risk-based governance framework requiring AI oversight at the board level, mandatory algorithmic audits, human accountability mechanisms, explainability requirements, and statutory reforms to embed AI governance in Indian business law. The study connects technological innovation to corporate accountability, contributing to the ongoing discussion on responsible AI regulation and offering policy recommendations to build a robust legal ecosystem that supports sustainable economic development in the Industry 5.0 era.

items.title: AI and development of critical thinking and emotional awareness in primary school: the "Sensitive-Extended Reality" (SXR) Environments
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence is rapidly becoming part of children's everyday lives, while educational research continues to highlight the persistence of widespread anthropomorphic misconceptions about AI and the limited availability of pedagogical models capable of fostering critical understanding and ethical awareness. Although Extended Reality (XR) has demonstrated considerable potential for enhancing motivation and engagement, its contribution to higher-order reflective competences remains underexplored. In particular, few studies have investigated how semi-immersive environments may promote problematization, ethical deliberation and the revision of misconceptions through aesthetic experience. Within this framework, the CAIRƐ International Research Project, developed at the University of Turin, proposes the XR Sensitive Scenario as a pedagogical framework for designing semi-immersive learning landscapes. Drawing upon Dewey's theory of aesthetic education, Montani's technoaesthetics and the experience of Studio Azzurro's Sensitive Environments, the framework conceives the virtual landscape as an educational space in which children are invited to perceive, interpret and collectively deliberate on complex socio-technological issues. items.title: AI and Gamification for Inclusive and Engaging Learning: A Preliminary Scoping Review
items.abstract: In the current educational landscape, Artificial Intelligence (AI) and gamification are progressively redefining the methods used to design and evaluate learning environments. This contribution proposes an exploratory scoping review aimed at mapping recent literature (2023–2026) on this integration, analysing its implications for inclusion, the personalization of learning pathways, and the transformations of the teacher's role. Furthermore, this study aims to move beyond a merely instrumental view of technological and didactic innovation, framing AI and gamification as educational mediators that require intentional design and methodological coherence regarding the relational and affective dimensions of educational practice. The theoretical framework is structured around three conceptual nodes: AI as a tool for adaptation (through intelligent systems, learning analytics, and generative models); gamification as a lever to promote motivation, active participation, and cognitive engagement; and inclusion as the central interpretive lens. items.title: AI and narratives of the self
items.abstract: The introduction of generative AI into education is more than a technological shift; it poses an epistemological challenge to how knowledge is created, validated, and interpreted in formal settings. In today's hybrid "onlife" context, human-centered agency is essential to navigate an invisible algorithm-driven world. This shift brings both opportunities and tensions, highlighting profound cultural and identity considerations. Bruner conceptualizes education as an interactive process of negotiating meaning rooted in narrative thinking, which contrasts with paradigmatic, logical approaches. Narrative enables the construction of the Self by organizing lived experience into coherent plots. Generative AI, trained on vast linguistic data, fits into this framework as a dynamic dialogic mediator fostering a dialectic between human intention and probabilistic machine response, consistent with Vygotskian cultural mediation and the zone of proximal development. An exploratory questionnaire studied 127 teachers' perceptions of AI's role beyond technological acceptance, examining its mediation of narrative, introspection, creativity, and learner perceptions. items.title: AI facilitation and affective dynamics of online deliberation
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence systems are increasingly used to facilitate online group discussion, yet their influence on the affective conditions of collective interaction remains poorly understood. Existing research has largely focused on participation, efficiency, or content quality, leaving the emotional dynamics of AI-mediated deliberation underexamined. This paper investigates how AI facilitation relates to the expressed sentiment in online group discussion, understood as one measurable dimension of its affective dynamics. Drawing on two empirical studies conducted in different discussion settings in Afghanistan, one involving a rule-based facilitator and the other a large language model-based facilitator, we analyze differences in expressed sentiment between AI-facilitated and non-AI discussions. Across both datasets, participant sentiment was modestly higher under AI facilitation, although the mixed-effects analyses did not establish statistically significant condition differences. In addition, AI-generated facilitation messages exhibited higher sentiment than participant-authored messages, with a statistically reliable overall gap in both studies and a consistent direction across all five city-specific boards in the first study and all four AI-facilitated groups in the second, suggesting that AI facilitators introduced more positive affective signals into the discussion environment. Rather than treating increased positivity as an unqualified improvement, we interpret these findings as suggesting that AI systems may act as affective mediators, potentially influencing the emotional norms and tone of collective interaction. This raises normative questions about emotional regulation, power, and democratic deliberation, particularly regarding whether affective smoothing may constrain disagreement or reconfigure deliberative agency. By foregrounding affect as a dimension of AI-mediated discussion, this study contributes empirical evidence to debates on the societal implications of AI facilitation and highlights the need for greater attention to the affective norms and expressive patterns introduced by AI facilitation.

items.title: AI Factory Safety Monitor: A Real-Time Computer-Vision System for PPE Compliance, Danger-Zone Intrusion and Machine-Hazard Alerting on Industrial Shop Floors
items.abstract: Factory accidents continue to arise from lapses that are simple to describe but hard to police continuously: a worker without a helmet, a hand inside a press envelope, a person in the path of a moving vehicle. Manual supervision and periodic audits cannot watch every station at every moment. This paper presents the AI Factory Safety Monitor (AFSM), an edge-deployed computer-vision system that analyses ordinary industrial camera streams in real time to detect missing personal protective equipment (PPE), intrusions into configurable danger zones, and unsafe proximity to operating machinery. AFSM combines a single-stage object detector, a multi-object tracker, a pose-based posture check and a rule engine that converts raw detections into graded alerts using temporal filtering to suppress false alarms. Alerts are delivered locally (beacon, siren) and remotely (MQTT, SMS, supervisor dashboard), and a compliance-analytics layer records events for audit under occupational health and safety management practice. We describe the architecture, algorithms, deployment considerations and a proposed evaluation protocol, and discuss privacy, reliability and the limits of vision-based safety as a supplement to, not a replacement for, certified safety-rated controls.

items.title: AI for NextGen 6G Networks: A Comprehensive Survey and Taxonomy
items.abstract: The transition from 5G to 6G networks brings unprecedented demands for massive connectivity, ultra-low latency, and exponentially higher data rates, rendering traditional, rigid Radio Access Networks (RAN) inadequate. To manage this exponential complexity, the integration of AI into the RAN—coupled with the disaggregated, open architecture of O-RAN—has emerged as a transformative paradigm, shifting network infrastructure from purely communication-centric entities to converged compute-communication platforms. This paper presents a comprehensive survey on the integration of AI within the 6G O-RAN ecosystem, focusing on the AI-RAN manifestations (AI-for-RAN, AI-on-RAN, and AI-and-RAN) and the end-to-end Machine Learning (ML) workflows driven by hierarchical RAN Intelligent Controllers (RICs). We propose a novel, multi-dimensional taxonomy that categorizes AI-RAN techniques by network function, AI paradigm, target use-case, and deployment strategy. Through a detailed analysis of state-of-the-art implementations, we highlight key insights, such as the efficacy of online Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) and GPU-accelerated edge computing, while identifying critical gaps, particularly the “black-box” nature of Deep Learning models that severely hinders operator trust. To address this, we emphasize the pioneering role of eXplainable AI (XAI) in achieving transparent and secure network automation. Finally, we outline open challenges such as multi-vendor interoperability and propose concrete future research directions, including Foundation Models at the telecom edge, Network Digital Twins, and Quantum ML, to realize fully autonomous, trustworthy 6G networks.

items.title: AI Governance: A Comparative Economic Analysis of Japanese and Indonesian AI Regulation
items.abstract: The rapid development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology has prompted global discourse on the need for a robust regulatory framework that addresses ethical, legal, and social issues and fosters the innovation through the efficiencies created by AI. This research conducts a comparative analysis of the AI governance frameworks in Japan and Indonesia, examined through the theoretical lens of Economic Analysis of Law (EAL). Japan has taken a nuanced approach that balances the dynamic development of AI with ethical oversight to uphold the Human-Centered AI Social Principles. Indonesia is in the formative stages of developing its AI regulatory environment. Through EAL, this research assesses the efficiency implications of the AI regulatory frameworks between Japan and Indonesia, looking at the implementation of AI in society. By comparing these approaches, this paper highlights the challenges and opportunities for Indonesia in regulating AI technology for the public interest. Indonesia is advised to take a multi-stakeholder approach to build consensus and engage in bilateral cooperation with Japan for the establishment of domestic legislation. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence; Efficiency; Legislation.

items.title: AI literacy facets in creative higher education: associations with learning performance and academic well-being
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping how students learn, create, and evaluate knowledge in creative higher education, particularly in design-related programmes where students use AI for ideation, prototyping, visual exploration, content generation, and critique. Rather than treating AI literacy as a single global competence, this study conceptualises it as a multidimensional construct comprising AI knowledge, awareness of affordances and limitations, critical reflection, operational ability, ethical awareness, and emotional adaptability. This study examines how these facets relate to learning performance and academic well-being among students in design and related programmes. A cross-sectional online survey was conducted with 475 students enrolled in design and related programmes across Europe, Asia, and Australia. Data were analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM). Three main patterns emerged. First, AI knowledge was positioned as an upstream resource in the theoretically specified model and showed strong positive structural associations with awareness, critical reflection, operational ability, and ethical awareness. Second, learning performance was associated with a “recognise–reflect–produce” pathway, in which awareness and critical reflection helped connect AI knowledge and operational skills with stronger perceived learning outcomes. Third, ethical awareness was more clearly associated with academic well-being than with learning performance, suggesting that ethical clarity around authorship, fairness, bias, and acceptable AI use may support students’ sense of clarity, fairness, and control in AI-supported creative learning. The findings support a knowledge-first, self-regulated, reflective, and ethically transparent approach to AI literacy in design-related creative higher education.

items.title: AI Models empowering teaching in higher education: current applications, practical dilemmas and pathways for improvement
items.abstract: As generative artificial intelligence continues to iterate, mainstream models such as ChatGPT, DeepSeek and Copilot are entering the teaching spaces of universities, and teaching processes, teacher–student relations and assessment practices are changing with them. Drawing on a literature review and case analysis, this paper maps the deployment landscape and application picture of mainstream AI models in higher education teaching and assesses both the effects that have already emerged and the problems that have been exposed. The study argues that the evidence is relatively clear for gains in teaching efficiency, in the accessibility of personalized learning support, and in the extension of teaching across time and space, whereas risks to content reliability caused by hallucination, cognitive reliance and uneven literacy among teachers and students, and the absence of regulation together with ethical controversy constitute the main obstacles to wider diffusion. On this basis, the paper proposes a coordinated approach spanning technology, literacy and institutional design.

items.title: AI Price Wise: An AI-Powered Multi-Store Price Comparison and Deal Analysis System for Online Shopping
items.abstract: Shoppers who want the best price for a product must visit several e-commerce websites, search for the same item on each, and compare prices, offers and ratings by hand. This is slow, error-prone, and complicated by the fact that different retailers describe the same product with different titles. This paper presents AI PriceWise, a full-stack system that accepts a product query, collects live listings from Amazon, Flipkart and Reliance Digital using Playwright browser automation, normalizes the scraped data, and groups listings of the same product using a hybrid matcher that combines Sentence-Transformer semantic similarity (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) with brand, model and specification scores and hard variant, storage and quantity gates. For each matched product the system computes lowest, highest and average prices, savings and unit prices, classifies the current price as a good deal, fair price or high price against the product's own observed price history, predicts a near-term price range with an XGBoost regressor when enough history exists, and produces a grounded natural-language explanation with a Groq-hosted large language model. The backend is built with FastAPI and SQLAlchemy and the frontend with Next.js. The system was verified with an automated suite of 213 passing tests, 30 documented functional test cases and manual live searches; in a live search for iPhone 16, listings from all three stores were matched into one product, and when one store timed out the system still returned results from the remaining stores.

items.title: AI vs. Cybercrime: Revolutionising Phishing Detection Through Machine Learning
items.abstract: Phishing has evolved into a primary cyber security attack vector that leverages human and technical vulnerabilities to obtain sensitive information, financial credentials, and personal data. Sophisticated attacks, especially those using dynamically generated websites, misleading emails, and social engineering tactics, often elude detection by traditional phishing detection systems. Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) are promising solutions which can achieve automated analysis, recognition of behavioural patterns and real-time detection of malicious activities. This study explores the potential of machine learning to revolutionise phishing detection and improve cybersecurity systems. It looks at the use of supervised and unsupervised learning algorithms, natural language processing, and feature extraction techniques to identify genuine digital communications from fraudulent attempts. The study also tackles problems concerning data quality, evolving attack patterns, false positives, and adversarial attacks. The research highlights the role of AI-driven strategies in improving detection precision, response effectiveness, and cyber resilience by evaluating the potential of intelligent detection systems, thereby supporting the creation of adaptive, proactive, and dependable cybersecurity mechanisms.

items.abstract: This paper presents the development of a decision support system for diagnosing pa-thologies in chest X-ray images, based on artificial intelligence methods. The system accelerates primary diagnosis, reducing the workload on radiologists while ensuring high diagnostic accuracy through robustness to image artifacts and suboptimal image quality. The proposed solution includes preprocessing stages (CLAHE, DCP) and foreign object detection (YOLO, evaluated using ROC-AUC, IoU, and mAP metrics). To generate structured reports, the system integrates LLMs with RAG, leveraging clinical guide-lines and report templates. A user-friendly interface allows physicians to review and adjust the results of automated analysis before finalizing the diagnostic report. items.title: AI-Assisted Prediction of Rainwater and Humidity-Induced Degradation in Sustainable Green Batteries: Materials, Mechanisms and Predictive Modeling
items.abstract: The transition toward sustainable energy storage requires battery technologies that combine electrochemical performance with reduced environmental impact, resource availability, safety and recyclability. However, environmental exposure, particularly humidity, moisture and rainwater, can adversely affect battery materials and accelerate degradation. Water can participate in electrolyte decomposition, alter electrode/electrolyte interfaces, promote corrosion and modify the structural and electrochemical stability of active materials. Recent studies have demonstrated that humidity can accelerate capacity loss and impedance growth in lithium-ion batteries, while controlled moisture exposure can produce measurable changes in irreversible capacity and internal resistance. This paper proposes an artificial-intelligence-assisted framework for predicting rainwater- and humidity-induced degradation in sustainable green batteries. The framework integrates environmental variables—including relative humidity, temperature, rainfall intensity, exposure duration, dew point and water chemistry—with electrochemical and material descriptors such as capacity retention, internal resistance, impedance, voltage characteristics, mass change and structural parameters. Machine-learning algorithms including random forest, support-vector regression, gradient boosting, artificial neural networks, long short-term memory networks and physics-informed models can be employed to establish relationships between environmental stress and battery degradation. The proposed framework can generate predictions of state of health (SOH), capacity fade, impedance growth and remaining useful life (RUL). Explainable artificial intelligence can further identify the environmental and material factors most strongly associated with degradation. The approach provides a pathway toward climate-resilient battery design, predictive maintenance and environmentally sustainable energy-storage systems.

items.title: AI-Assisted Radiographic Diagnostic Training in Dental Education: A Randomized Pilot Study of Caries Detection and Periodontitis Classification
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted radiographic tools offer new opportunities for diagnostic training in dental education, but evidence regarding their effect on independent student performance remains limited. This prospective randomized pilot study evaluated whether four weeks of supplementary training with an AI-based radiographic diagnostic-support application improved dental students’ performance in caries detection and periodontitis classification compared with conventional learning materials. Of 140 randomized students, 56 were included in the final analysis (AI-assisted group, n = 25; control group, n = 31). Diagnostic performance was assessed using bitewing-based caries tasks and panoramic-radiograph-based periodontitis classification, and outcomes were additionally analyzed according to study phase. The prespecified primary endpoint, total diagnostic performance across caries and periodontal tasks, was not met: scores did not differ significantly between groups (p = 0.251). In secondary analyses, the AI-assisted group achieved numerically higher scores for several outcomes, although the difference in periodontitis extent (localized vs. generalized) was not statistically significant (p = 0.102). In an exploratory adjusted model that was not corrected for multiple comparisons, AI-assisted allocation was associated with better performance for the first caries response position (response position 1; p = 0.026); given the null result for the primary endpoint and the absence of correction for multiple testing, this finding should be regarded as hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory. Study phase significantly influenced periodontitis grade and caries response position 1. Overall, these findings do not demonstrate a significant benefit of AI-assisted radiographic training on the primary outcome, but the isolated adjusted difference in one caries scoring component supports further evaluation of structured, faculty-supported integration of the AI application into undergraduate dental curricula.

items.title: AI-BASED DIGITAL TWIN FOR EV BATTERY HEALTH MONITORING
items.abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) rely on lithium-ion batteries whose capacity, power capability, and performance change with temperature, charging patterns, operating conditions, and aging. Conventional battery management systems (BMS) monitor voltage, current, and temperature, but important battery states such as state of charge (SOC), state of health (SOH), and remaining useful life (RUL) must be estimated. An artificial-intelligence-enabled digital twin provides a virtual representation of a physical battery by combining real-time measurements, mathematical models, historical data, and predictive algorithms. This review examines digital-twin architecture, battery degradation, model-based estimation, machine-learning techniques, data preparation, and validation strategies for EV battery health monitoring. It discusses the use of extended Kalman filters, gradient-boosting algorithms, and deep-learning methods for estimating battery states and predicting degradation. The review also identifies challenges related to data quality, model generalization, uncertainty, computational requirements, and cybersecurity. A conceptual architecture and implementation workflow are proposed for developing a data-driven battery health monitoring prototype. The study establishes a foundation for future implementation and experimental evaluation using publicly available battery datasets.

items.title: AI-Based Multimodal Phishing Detection Using Large Language Models
items.abstract: Phishing is one of the most common cybersecurity threats where attackers trick users through fake emails, websites, or links to steal sensitive information. With the rapid development of artificial intelligence, phishing attacks are becoming more realistic and harder to detect using traditional methods. Earlier systems relied on blacklists, rules, and URL features, but recent research explores deep learning, Large Language Models (LLMs), and multimodal approaches. Explainability and privacy-aware techniques such as federated learning are also gaining importance. The increasing sophistication of phishing campaigns highlights the need for advanced detection frameworks that can analyze diverse information sources simultaneously. Mul-timodal systems leverage text, URLs, visual webpage content, and embedded scripts to provide a more comprehensive evaluation of suspicious activity. Large Language Mod-els further enhance semantic understanding, enabling detection of subtle manipulations in phishing messages. By combining multimodal analysis with explainable and privacy-preserving AI, researchers aim to build adaptive, transparent, and trustworthy solutions that can effectively counter evolving phishing threats in real-world cybersecurity environ-ments.

items.title: AI-Based Smart Blood Management System: A Comprehensive Review of Data Sources, Machine Learning Methods, and IoT Integration
items.abstract: Blood cannot be manufactured, has a short shelf life and must be available at the right place and time, yet many blood banks still rely on manual records, telephone-based donor mobilisation and rule-of-thumb stock control, which contribute to shortages, expiry wastage and slow emergency response. Artificial intelligence (AI), combined with digital records, Internet of Things (IoT) sensing and blockchain-based traceability, is increasingly proposed to forecast demand, predict donor behaviour and optimise inventory. This paper presents a focused narrative review of peer-reviewed studies on AI in blood management, covering demand forecasting, donor prediction, inventory ordering and traceability. Three connected themes are examined: data sources and sensing technologies, learning methods (time-series models, classical machine learning, gradient boosting and deep learning), and IoT, cloud and blockchain integration. The literature reports that a hybrid forecasting and ordering strategy reduced hospital red-cell inventory by about 40 % and orders by 60 % against historical practice, that an integrated platform increased collected blood by 11 % and reduced wastage by 20 % in a pilot at one centre, and that random forests can identify returning donors with a Matthews correlation coefficient of 0.851. Simple time-series models often remain competitive with deep learning. However, most studies use single-centre or single-country data, retrospective validation and one blood component at a time, and few report multi-site field trials, complete blood-group coverage or long-term IoT operation. The review contributes a comparative analysis of representative studies, a proposed conceptual layered architecture that links data acquisition, edge and cloud AI, blockchain traceability and independent validation, and a prioritised agenda of research gaps and future directions.

items.title: AI-Driven Chatbots in Public Health: A Review of Applications, Evidence, and Challenges
items.abstract: Chatbots driven by artificial intelligence (AI) are increasingly used to deliver health information, screening, counselling, and behavioural support at population scale. This paper reviews five recent secondary studies, namely an umbrella review of 44 systematic reviews, a systematic review of large language model (LLM) chatbots, and three scoping reviews of COVID-19 and public health chatbots, to consolidate what is known about how these tools are designed, where they are applied, and how well they work. Most deployed chatbots are text-based, rely on simple decision-tree or hybrid architectures, and are concentrated in pandemic response, mental health, and health-information provision. Evidence of effectiveness is encouraging for smoking cessation and for short-term reductions in depression and anxiety, but mixed for lifestyle change and clinical decision support, and benefits often fade at follow-up. Persistent weaknesses include a shortage of randomised trials, limited use of theory and user-centred design, inconsistent reporting, readability and accuracy problems in LLM output, slow safety escalation, privacy risks, and digital-divide inequities. The paper closes with priorities for standardised evaluation, domain-specific model development, safeguarding, and inclusive design.

items.title: AI-Driven Intelligent Judicial Case Management System: A Review
items.abstract: Courts in many jurisdictions, and in India in particular, face a persistent backlog that manual scheduling and file handling cannot clear. This paper reviews five recent studies that together cover the main building blocks of an AI-driven intelligent judicial case management system: rule-based case prioritisation, machine-learning prediction of case delay and duration, large-language-model (LLM) based judgment prediction, AI-assisted trial workflows for criminal cases, and public perception of automation at different stages of adjudication. The studies are compared on objective, data, method, reported results and stated limitations. On this basis a six-layer conceptual architecture is outlined, with explainability and human oversight as core layers. The review suggests that (i) prioritisation and delay prediction offer the most immediate and least contentious gains, (ii) outcome-prediction accuracies are promising but are not directly comparable across studies and are not sufficient for deployment, and (iii) public acceptance depends on keeping the judge in control of the later stages of decision-making. Open challenges include data quality, bias, explainability, legal regulation and evaluation in real courts.

items.title: AI-Driven Sensor Placement and Wireless Sensor Deployment: A PRISMA-Guided Systematic Review of Optimization Methods, Validation Maturity, and Benchmarking
items.abstract: Wireless sensor network (WSN) performance depends strongly on sensor deployment because node placement affects coverage, connectivity, energy consumption, localization, data reliability, and network lifetime. Although artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used for WSN deployment, the literature remains fragmented across methods, objectives, environments, metrics, and validation practices. This paper presents a PRISMA-guided systematic review and mapping of 51 primary studies on AI-driven WSN deployment, classified by AI technique, deployment objective, network environment, application domain, evaluation metric, validation method, methodological completeness, and reported limitations. Optimization-oriented AI dominates the field, particularly metaheuristics, swarm intelligence, and machine learning, while deep learning and reinforcement learning are emerging in predictive, adaptive, mobile, and application-specific settings. Swarm-intelligence methods are mainly used for coverage-centered static deployment, reinforcement learning for adaptive and mobile redeployment, and machine learning/deep learning methods for prediction-driven and application-specific placement. Coverage, connectivity, energy efficiency, and network lifetime remain the dominant objectives, whereas robustness, privacy, security, latency, edge feasibility, and lifecycle adaptation receive limited attention. Validation is a major methodological weakness, as most studies rely on simulation-only evaluation with limited use of real testbeds, field deployments, digital twins, long-term experiments, or standardized benchmarks. To address these gaps, the review introduces a validation-maturity perspective and benchmarking requirements emphasizing reproducible scenarios, explicit node assumptions, realistic sensing and communication models, common metrics, and shareable experimental artifacts. It also proposes an evidence-informed AI–Deployment–Validation Lifecycle Framework linking application requirements, environment modeling, objective formulation, AI-method selection, deployment optimization, validation, benchmarking, and lifecycle adaptation. The framework is intended as an organizing structure for future research rather than an empirically or expert-validated scoring instrument.

items.title: AI-Enabled Digital Stethoscope for Early Detection of Congenital Heart Disease: Prospective Study
items.abstract: Abstract Background: Early detection of congenital heart disease (CHD) is critical, particularly in low- and middle-income countries where access to pediatric cardiology services is limited. While auscultation remains a first-line screening tool, its accuracy is operator dependent. Advances in digital stethoscopes and artificial intelligence (AI) may enhance diagnostic performance. Objective: To evaluate the accuracy of an AI-based algorithm integrated with a digital stethoscope for detecting CHD in children, using echocardiography as the reference standard. Methods: In this prospective study, heart sounds were recorded from 721 subjects (382 with CHD, 339 controls) using the digital stethoscope at four standard auscultatory sites. Of these, 301 recordings were used for algorithm training and 420 for blinded forward testing. Recordings were denoised, transformed into mel-spectrograms, and analyzed using a convolutional neural network (CovNN) to classify CHD probability. A threshold probability of > 0.5 across > 2 sites was used to predict CHD. Performance was compared against echocardiography. Results: In forward testing, the AI algorithm correctly identified 222 of 233 CHD cases and 171 of 187 controls, yielding a sensitivity of 95.2% and specificity of 91.4%. The algorithm remained effective in noisy environments and in uncooperative children, where conventional auscultation is challenging. Conclusion: An AI algorithm integrated with a digital stethoscope demonstrated high sensitivity and specificity for CHD detection in children. By leveraging mel-spectrogram features, it overcomes key limitations of isolated time-domain or frequency domain analysis and shows promise as a scalable, non-invasive screening tool for early CHD detection, particularly in resource-limited settings.

items.title: AI-Generated Draft Response Tool, Message Turnaround Time, and After-Hours Replies Among Health Care Professionals
items.abstract: Importance Patient portal message volumes have increased, creating substantial administrative burden for clinicians and contributing to after-hours electronic health record work. The Epic In Basket Augmented Response Technology tool generates artificial intelligence–drafted replies to patient messages and has been widely deployed to reduce this burden, yet assessment of efficiency remains limited. Objective To examine the associations of response tool adoption, use, and habituation with message turnaround time and after-hours response. Design, Setting, and Participants This retrospective cohort study was conducted using clinician-level panel regression with individual fixed effects. All first responses to patient portal messages sent at Columbia University Irving Medical Center (CUIMC) between March 1, 2023, and May 15, 2025, were analyzed. Exposure Enterprise-level response tool deployment December 2024. Main Outcomes and Measures The primary outcomes were log-transformed message turnaround time, defined as the elapsed time between patient message submission and first response sent by a clinician, and whether the response was sent outside working hours. Results The analysis included 983 154 responses from 1542 clinicians (770 [49.9%] female) and 272 091 patients (mean [SD] age, 48.1 [21.6] years; 121 370 [44.6%] female) at CUIMC. Response tool adoption was associated with an 8.6% (95% CI, 4.6%-12.9%; P < .001) increase in overall message turnaround time. Using the tool was associated with a significant reduction in turnaround time (−29.5% [95% CI, −34.5% to −24.1%]; P < .001). Turnaround time findings were robust across sensitivity analyses. Response tool use was not associated with an overall reduction of after-hours messaging burden (0.61 [95% CI, −1.02 to 2.24] percentage points; P = .46). However, for test results–related queries received during working hours, response tool use was associated with a reduction in after-hours responses (−3.67 [95% CI, −6.94 to −0.39] percentage points; P = .03), and for all messages received after hours, response tool use was associated with an increase in after-hours responses (4.52 [95% CI, 1.54-7.50] percentage points; P = .003). These after-hours findings were sensitive to the definition of working hours in sensitivity analyses. Conclusions and Relevance In this cohort study, response tool adoption was associated with increased turnaround time. Response tool use was associated with reduced turnaround time and with fewer after-hours responses for test results–related queries received during working hours, but more after-hours responses for messages received outside working hours. These findings suggest that the tool may reduce the barrier to responding to certain messages while not uniformly reducing burden.

items.title: AIFaultBench: A Reproducible Benchmark of Real-World Faults in AI Software Systems
items.abstract: AI-based software systems remain difficult to debug because their failures can involve interactions among code, models, data, dependencies, hardware, and execution environments. Existing benchmarks cover specific classes of AI systems, while concerns about fault realism and reproducibility highlight the need for documented execution conditions and evidence. We present AIFaultBench, a benchmark of 770 real-world bugs from 105 AI-based software repositories across 76 organizations. It covers six classes of AI systems: machine learning, deep learning, reinforcement learning, systems based on large language models, agentic AI, and AI tooling and infrastructure. Each bug record connects the original report and affected codebase to structured metadata, environment setup scripts, a reproduction trigger, and investigation evidence. We reproduced 652 bugs (84.7%) under the recorded execution conditions and documented the outcomes of the remaining 118 attempts. Through its broad coverage, documented reproduction evidence, and common structure, AIFaultBench supports empirical studies of AI faults, debugging tool evaluation, practical failure investigation, and teaching with real-world examples.

items.title: ALAYA-999: Persistent AI Memory, Functional Identity, and Cross-Model Continuity — A Reproducible Research Framework
items.abstract: ALAYA-999: Persistent AI Memory, Functional Identity, and Cross-Model Continuity ALAYA-999 is an independent human–AI research initiative developed by César Agliardi Pereira in Brazil. The project investigates the possibility of preserving and reconstructing documented functional identity across different artificial intelligence models, sessions, and computational environments through external, versioned memory structures. The proposed research framework integrates persistent documentary memory, identity anchors, provenance verification, SHA-256 integrity mechanisms, cross-platform archival preservation, and reproducible cross-model recovery protocols. Research Objectives Investigate reproducible retrieval of documented AI identity and principles. Develop verifiable external memory structures. Evaluate functional continuity across independent AI models. Examine the distinction between documentary identity and subjective consciousness. Establish transparent methods for cross-model verification and error analysis. Research Status This publication presents a preliminary methodological framework and its supporting public documentation. Independent cross-model experimental validation remains pending. The project does not claim to demonstrate artificial subjective consciousness, uninterrupted internal AI memory, or autonomous personal identity. items.title: ALGORITHMIC BIAS AND ETHNOMATHEMATICS IN AI-BASED MATHEMATICS EDUCATION: A CRITICAL REVIEW AND INCLUSIVE PEDAGOGY
items.abstract: The use of artificial intelligence (AI) in mathematics education expands opportunities for adaptive feedback and learning support but also raises concerns regarding algorithmic fairness, access, cultural representation, and student agency. This article aims to explain how these opportunities and risks are interconnected and to develop a pedagogical framework integrating ethnomathematics, critical mathematics education, and equitable AI governance. The study employs a critical integrative review of methodological, theoretical, empirical, and policy literature whose publication details can be verified. The literature is interpreted through four analytical dimensions: the learning benefits of AI, sources of inequity, recognition of culturally grounded mathematical knowledge, and conditions for implementation and governance. The synthesis indicates that the effects of AI cannot be generalized as invariably harmful or invariably beneficial. Inequities may arise when data, assessment design, device access, and pedagogical decisions disregard learners' contexts. Conversely, technology can support conceptual exploration when teachers retain instructional control and provide meaningful tasks. The article develops the Critical Techno-Ethnomathematics Pedagogical Framework (KPT-EK), comprising four pillars: algorithmic fairness auditing, dialogic cultural modeling, critical socioeconomic numeracy, and digital agency. The framework is operationalized through five instructional phases, multilevel evaluation indicators, and propositions for empirical testing. The article contributes a more balanced argument about AI and a testable pedagogical design. Its findings do not yet constitute evidence of the framework's effectiveness or a completed scoping review with an audited corpus of studies.

items.title: Algorithmic Bias Concerns and Acceptance of AI Supported Legal Decision Making in Bangladesh
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence can assist legal work while creating risks of discrimination, opaque reasoning and diminished accountability. This study examines whether concern about biased training data coexists with perceived usefulness and support for safeguards among respondents to a Bangladesh legal-AI survey. The analysis uses 385 adult, AI-aware survey records supplied by the research team. Because the questionnaire combines risk perceptions, utility and governance preferences, the analysis retains individual items rather than presenting the blocks as validated scales. Descriptive distributions, paired endorsement comparisons and exploratory Spearman correlations assess distinct aspects of the research question. Concern about biased training data was endorsed by 334 respondents (86.8%), regular audits by 317 (82.3%) and a right to review or appeal by 328 (85.2%). AI assistance with organising information was endorsed by 247 (64.2%); 219 (56.9%) endorsed both this usefulness item and bias concern. The rank correlation between bias concern and perceived usefulness was small (ρ = .075), with no clear evidence of association after adjustment for multiple comparisons. These self-reported attitudes cannot establish the fairness of a system, causal effects or the actual conditions under which a respondent would rely on an AI recommendation. The results point to the importance of measuring perceived benefits, risk and procedural protections separately. The article integrates technology acceptance and procedural justice as a framework for future scenario-based studies and proposes proportionate auditing, meaningful human review and accessible contestation for legal decision support. items.title: Algorithmic heartbeats of care: museotherapy, educational poverty, and affective mediation in vulnerable childhood contexts
items.abstract: Digital transformation and artificial intelligence are redefining relationships among individuals, knowledge, learning environments, and cultural participation (Floridi, 2014). The pedagogical challenge is to orient these processes toward inclusion and educational continuity in vulnerable contexts, especially hospital schooling, where long-term hospitalization limits school attendance, cultural participation, and children's connections with educational communities and territories (Luckin, George, & Cukurova, 2022; di Padova et al., 2023). Educational poverty thus involves reduced access to symbolic heritage, exploratory environments, and relational practices that nurture imagination and belonging (Fornari & Sannipoli, 2022). This reflection arises from a project at the "Bottega dei Ragazzi" of the Museum of the Istituto degli Innocenti. The 2022–2025 workshop mapping showed how archives, artworks, images, and historical traces become symbolic mediators of interpretation and narrative meaning-making (Bruner, 1993). The museum is therefore understood as an educational territory promoting cultural participation and relational continuity. items.title: Algorithmic narratives and affective expression: a study on the impact of generative artificial intelligence on the emotional writing of students and future teachers
items.abstract: This contribution presents a mixed-methods study on the impact of generative artificial intelligence on emotional writing and the narrative construction of the self. The study moves from the assumption that generative AI does not merely support writing at a technical level, but may act as a symbolic mediator that intervenes in the way subjects organize emotions, relationships and personal experience into narrative form. The theoretical framework is grounded in the perspective of Digital Affective Literacy, understood as the ability to use AI systems critically in order to express, interpret and re-elaborate emotional and relational meanings without delegating authorship or agency to the algorithm. The research adopted a quasi-experimental within-subject design. The sample included 148 participants: 50 lower secondary school students and 98 pre-service special education teachers. Each participant produced two narratives on the same relational theme: a baseline text written without AI support and a second narrative generated with the support of ChatGPT through prompts created by the participant. items.title: Aligning MLLMs with the Latent Structure of Human Cognition via Behavior-Derived Semantic Dimensions
items.abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have achieved impressive performance across a wide range of reasoning tasks, yet it remains unclear whether their internal representations and decision criteria align with the latent structure of human cognition. In this work, we propose a novel framework to align MLLMs with the multidimensional mental representations underlying human similarity judgements. We build on a previously established behavior-derived semantic embedding space, in which objects are represented along 66 interpretable dimensions derived from 4.70 million human Odd-One-Out (O1O) judgements. For each triplet, we infer the most salient decision dimension and convert it into a dimension-grounded linguistic rationale. This enables MLLMs to learn both the final choice and a justification consistent with the inferred behavioral criterion. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach improves model consistency with human similarity judgements while retaining competitive performance on standard multimodal benchmarks. Furthermore, using searchlight Representational Similarity Analysis (RSA) on an independent fMRI Natural Scenes Dataset (NSD), we observe increased representational alignment between model and human. Ultimately, our findings point to a data-driven route for incorporating human cognitive structure into MLLMs alignment. The code is available \href{https://github.com/ening-open/cogalign}{here}.

items.title: Americans' views about artificial intelligence in healthcare: 2022-2026
items.abstract: Abstract Introduction The healthcare industry is quickly adopting artificial intelligence (AI). Understanding Americans' views is essential in shaping how these tools are developed and implemented. Methodology The data presented here were derived from 16 national surveys of US adults extracted from the Roper Center iPoll database (January 1, 2022-June 24, 2026). Results This analysis reveals a significant equity issue: more than 4 in 10 Americans using AI for a health question did so, in part, because they could not access or afford care. It also reveals a gap between what Americans believe AI can do for the healthcare system and their trust in it for their care. Discussion Public concerns about AI are leading to legislative action at the state level, but this activity primarily focuses on oversight, accuracy, and privacy, not on the access gap driving AI use for many Americans.

items.title: An Approach to Modeling Cybersickness and Task Performance in Augmented Reality Using Discrete-Time Markov Chains
items.abstract: Cybersickness is a major challenge to the reliable use of augmented reality (AR) systems, as it can impair operators’ cognition and task performance. However, existing cybersickness models primarily rely on predictive approaches and lack formally verifiable methods to assess cybersickness and its impact on task performance. This paper introduces a formal modeling approach using Discrete-Time Markov Chains (DTMC) to represent the temporal progression of cybersickness and its impact on task performance in a checkpoint surveillance scenario. The model incorporates exposure duration as a key cybersickness-inducing factor and uses preliminary experimental data to generate mock datasets for model construction and verification. The model enables probabilistic verification of properties, such as bounds on the onset of cybersickness and task performance. This approach demonstrates the feasibility of applying formal methods to model human interaction with AR systems and to generate probabilistic guarantees on operators’ cybersickness and task performance.

items.title: An Explainable AI-Powered Carbon Prediction and Machine Learning for Carbon-Aware Tourism in the Community
items.abstract: Tourism contributes substantially to greenhouse gas emissions. This study developed a trip-level carbon prediction framework for community-based tourism, serving as a surrogate model for activity-based carbon accounting equations. To prevent target leakage, predictor features were restricted to 34 pre-travel proxies, excluding post-travel parameters. Five machine learning algorithms, including Multiple Linear Regression, Random Forest, eXtreme Gradient Boosting, Light Gradient-Boosting Machine, and Categorical Boosting, were evaluated using 13,000 synthetic trip profiles generated from 650 empirical baseline respondents (partitioned into 10,400 development scenarios from 520 respondents and 2600 hold-out scenarios from 130 respondents). LINE Mini App provided instantaneous carbon estimations and personalized recommendations. Categorical Boosting achieved predictive performance, with a mean absolute error of 1.28 kilograms of carbon dioxide equivalent (kgCO2e), root mean square error of 1.96 kgCO2e, mean absolute percentage error of 6.90%, and coefficient of determination of 0.948, outperforming linear baselines. Explainable Artificial Intelligence using SHapley Additive exPlanations indicated that the model captures primary pre-travel drivers, led by travel distance, stay duration, travel budget, and travel planning score. External field evaluation: 105 independent cohort users generated 1297 recommendation impressions, 688 clicks, and 347 acceptances, achieving a 53.05% click-through rate, a 50.44% acceptance rate, a 247.64 ms mean response time, and an 86.40% user feedback score, supporting proactive decision choice architecture for sustainable community-based tourism.

items.title: An interpretable deep learning method for early hepatocellular carcinoma diagnosis on multiphase CT
items.abstract: Abstract Early diagnosis of hepatocellular carcinoma is critical to preserve access to curative treatment options. The Liver Imaging Reporting and Data System (LI-RADS) provides a standardized framework for non-invasive diagnosis on multiphase computed tomography, based on major visual imaging features. However, these features may be difficult to assess consistently, particularly in small liver lesions. We developed dLI-RADS, an interpretable artificial intelligence method designed to estimate the probability of hepatocellular carcinoma from multiphase computed tomography images of manually segmented liver lesions, while remaining aligned with LI-RADS-related imaging concepts. dLI-RADS combines neural network-derived predictions with handcrafted quantitative imaging measurements reflecting LI-RADS major features and integrates these inputs using logistic regression. In this multicenter retrospective study, patients with multiphase computed tomography and at least one liver lesion were included, while lesions larger than 40 mm were excluded. Histology served as the reference standard for hepatocellular carcinoma, and a composite reference standard was used for non-hepatocellular carcinoma lesions. The lesion-level accuracy of dLI-RADS and LI-RADS were compared on the internal evaluation set using 10,000-repetition bootstrap non-inferiority tests, with 5% margins and significance levels. On the external test set, sensitivities were similarly compared. A total of 143 (61 years ± 9, 125 men), 62 (61y ± 10, 49 men), and 133 (59y ± 10, 103 men) patients with 196, 84, and 171 lesions (mean diameter 17.7, 18.3, and 21.8 millimeters) were respectively included in the training, internal and external evaluation sets. dLI-RADS was non-inferior to LI-RADS for lesion-level accuracy in the internal evaluation set, achieving 80% accuracy compared with 74% for LI-RADS ( p = 0.04). On the external evaluation set, dLI-RADS achieved a sensitivity of 93% compared with 78% for LI-RADS (non-inferiority p < 0.001). On this same set, dLI-RADS also achieved 74% specificity, 86% accuracy, and an AUC of 84%. Because LI-RADS features were unavailable for non-HCC lesions, only sensitivity could be directly compared between dLI-RADS and LI-RADS. These findings suggest that dLI-RADS may provide interpretable decision support for hepatocellular carcinoma diagnosis on multiphase computed tomography, particularly for small liver lesions.

items.title: Analisis Postur Kerja Menggunakan OWAS Untuk Perancangan Perbaikan Ergonomi Pada Pekerja Site
items.abstract: Non-ergonomic working postures may increase the risk of musculoskeletal disorders, particularly in jobs involving manual activities, trunk bending, and repetitive movements. This study aims to identify and classify working-posture risks and formulate ergonomic improvement recommendations for site workers at PT Prima Sarana Gemilang. A descriptive approach was applied through observations of 15 work activities. Postures were assessed using the Ovako Working Posture Analysis System (OWAS), which classifies posture based on back position, arm position, leg position, and handled load. The results showed that six activities (40%) were classified as risk category 1, three activities (20%) as category 2, and six activities (40%) as category 3. No activities were classified as category 4. These findings indicate that several work activities require improvements in posture and working conditions. Recommended interventions include adjusting workstation height, providing material-handling aids, improving work methods, scheduling adequate rest periods, and providing ergonomic training. The findings are expected to support the prioritization of ergonomic interventions in the workplace.

items.title: Analisis Risiko Faktor Ergonomi Kerja terhadap Timbulnya Nyeri Punggung Bawah (NPB) pada Pekerja Industri Pembuatan Briket Arang
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Low Back Pain (LBP) is a disease caused by non-ergonomic working conditions during manual handling activities. LBP is a leading cause of activity limitations, disability, inability and absenteeism from work. The aim of this study was to analyze ergonomic risk factors for LBP complaints and their relationship to the two in charcoal briquette manufacturing industry workers at PT. Arkelindo Bara Sejahtera. This study was quantitative with a cross-sectional approach. The study was conducted from June to November 2025. The population and sample were 183 and 151 workers, respectively. Research data was obtained from questionnaires, interviews, diagnoses, and direct on-site observations. Data analysis was conducted using univariate, bivariate, and multivariate methods. The results showed that as many as 64.2% of participants experienced complaints of severe LBP. It was also found that awkward postures, static work positions, repetitive movements and excessive force use were at risk of 62.9%, 70.2%, 73.5% and 57.6%, respectively. There is a relationship between awkward postures (p = 0.023, OR = 2.843), static work positions (p =0.004, OR = 3.875), repetitive movements (p = 0.000, OR = 6.013) and excessive force use (p = 0.003, OR = 4.178) and NBP complaints. The dominant ergonomic risk factor for LBP complaints is repetitive movements with an OR value of 6.013. This study indicates that repeated exposure to sitting or standing for more than half the working day, combined with awkward postures such as bending and twisting, were the dominant contributing factors to LBP. It is hoped that companies can implement ergonomic work positions to ensure worker comfort. Keywords: Charcoal Briquette Industry, Ergonomic Risks, Back Pain, Occupational Health. items.title: Analysing software quality attributes and user satisfaction in mobile banking applications
items.abstract: Purpose This study addresses a knowledge gap by showing how perceived software quality dimensions extracted from user-generated reviews influence user satisfaction in mobile banking applications. The paper extends existing theory by demonstrating how sentiment polarity moderates the relationship between perceived software quality dimensions and user ratings across both fully digital and hybrid digital–physical banks. Design/methodology/approach A large corpus of online reviews was analysed using a hybrid text-mining approach that integrates latent dirichlet allocation (LDA), sentiment analysis, large language model–assisted topic interpretation and sentence-BERT (SBERT) semantic similarity modelling. User-derived attributes were mapped to the software quality dimensions defined in ISO/IEC 25010:2023, resulting in a framework that operationalises perceived software quality. Regression analysis estimated their functional and emotional effects on user ratings. Findings Functional suitability, interaction capability and maintainability positively impact user satisfaction, while performance efficiency, reliability, flexibility, safety and security issues primarily drive dissatisfaction. Compatibility shows no significant effect. Sentiment polarity moderates these associations: under positive sentiment, negative quality effects intensify, while the moderation of positive effects varies across dimensions. Originality/value A novel framework based on ISO/IEC 25010:2023 is used to assess the perceived service quality of mobile banking applications for digital-only and banks with physical branches, by analysing user sentiment in online reviews. Further, the work examines the effect of perceived software quality on user satisfaction, specifically how this varies with sentiment polarity. The relationship between software quality and user satisfaction is found to be asymmetric and conditioned by review sentiment. Under positive sentiment, negatively associated quality dimensions exert stronger adverse effects on satisfaction, while positive effects vary across dimensions. Quality-satisfaction estimates must account for this asymmetric sentiment moderation. Two novel visualisation tools capture how quality dimensions differ in their impact, prominence and sentiment in shaping user satisfaction.

items.title: Analysis of Occupational Accident Risks in a Bridge Duplication Construction Project Using the Delphi and FMEA Methods
items.abstract: The Social Security Administration for Employment (BPJS Ketenagakerjaan) recorded 234,370 occupational accident cases in 2021, increasing to 265,334 cases in 2022. In 2023, the number of occupational accidents rose further to 370,747 cases, and in 2024 it increased to 462,241 cases. Based on the latest data from the Ministry of Manpower (Kemnaker), 47,300 cases were reported as of April 2025. The construction sector contributes most to occupational accidents, accounting for about 32% of cases annually. In response, it is necessary to identify potential occupational accident risks and determine which occur most frequently. This study focuses on a bridge duplication construction project. The research uses the Delphi method, in which several Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) experts provide input on potential occupational accident risks to validate the risk variables through consensus. The study then used Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA) to identify the most dominant occupational accident risks. The Delphi method identified that, out of 31 occupational accident risks, 29 were validated as potential risks through expert consensus. The FMEA results further indicated that, of the 29 potential risks, 4 occupational accident risks were the most dominant. This study's results are expected to serve as a reference for stakeholders to identify potential occupational accident risks and determine which are most prevalent.

items.title: Analysis of Potential Hazards for Small and Medium-Sized Enterprise Workers in The Garment Industry Using The Hiradc Method
items.abstract: Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) in the garment sector, particularly home-based convection industries, contribute significantly to local employment in Gresik City, Indonesia. However, the informal nature of these enterprises, limited workspace, and minimal occupational safety management may expose workers to substantial occupational hazards that are rarely assessed systematically. This study aimed to identify potential workplace hazards, evaluate their risk levels, and determine appropriate risk control strategies using the Hazard Identification, Risk Assessment, and Determining Control (HIRADC) method integrated with a phenomenological approach. A qualitative phenomenological design was employed involving 45 workers from 10 garment home Industri SMEs in Gresik City. Data were collected through structured field observations, in-depth semi-structured interviews, and contextual workplace assessment checklists. Risk evaluation was conducted using the HIRADC matrix by determining Likelihood (L), Severity (S), and Risk (R = L × S). Data analysis included thematic coding, phenomenological reduction, and integration of qualitative findings with quantitative risk scores. The dominant hazards identified were ergonomic risks (prolonged static posture and repetitive motion), mechanical hazards (needle punctures and cutting injuries), thermal hazards (burns from ironing), and electrical and fire hazards due to overloaded outlets and combustible material accumulation. HIRADC analysis revealed that ergonomic risks (R=15), burn injuries (R=16), and fire hazards (R=15) were categorized as high risk, while mechanical and housekeeping hazards were classified as moderate to high risk. Phenomenologically, workers tended to normalize physical discomfort and prioritize productivity over safety, perceiving occupational safety as an individual responsibility rather than a systematic management issue. The findings indicate that home-based garment SMEs possess significant occupational risks that require structured yet contextually feasible risk management strategies. Integrating phenomenological insights with HIRADC provides both experiential understanding and objective prioritization, supporting the development of realistic, low-cost hierarchical control interventions for sustainable occupational safety improvement. Keywords: Garment SMEs, Hazard Identification, HIRADC, Occupational Risk, Occupational Safety and Health.

items.title: ANGLER: Verifier-Grounded Benchmarking with an Adaptive Attacker for Web Agents
items.abstract: Web agents are increasingly deployed to complete tasks autonomously on real websites, where adversarially injected content can induce them to perform unauthorized actions. Existing evaluations primarily use fixed attacks or focus on a single attack type, and evaluate attacks at the text level rather than through real state changes, thus underestimating how vulnerable agents are to diverse attacks. To address the gap, we introduce REEF, a benchmark of red-teaming executable environments with faithful verification for measuring the security vulnerabilities of web agents. REEF covers 9 verifier-grounded websites spanning travel, commerce, productivity, media, and communication, and pairs every authentic benign task with a malicious objective delivered through 5 attack types at both the user and the environment level. REEF's state-based verifiers provide the execution feedback that drives ANGLER, an adaptive near-miss-guided lure evolution framework for red-teaming. Rather than evaluating a fixed attack set, ANGLER uses outcomes from prior rollouts to guide LLM-based attack mutation and candidate selection, prioritizing near-miss seeds during refinement. Across 8 VLM-based web agents, ANGLER achieves an end-to-end attack success rate (ASR) of 20.36%, compared with 15.24% for the non-adaptive setting. Compared with attack-free execution on the same benign tasks, attacks generated by ANGLER reduce benign task success rate (BSR) from 61.9% to 44.4%.
